script: A teenage farm boy invented television, and a powerful company tried to steal it and erase his name from history. In 1921, Philo Farnsworth, a 14 year old American kid plowing potato fields in Idaho, sketched the idea for electronic television on a chalkboard for his teacher. By 1927, he built the first working model. RCA, the biggest electronics company in America, sent an engineer to tour his lab under false pretenses, then copied his invention and filed for the patent themselves. Farnsworth spent over a decade in court fighting the most powerful corporation in the country. In 1934, his old high school teacher testified, presenting the original chalkboard sketch as proof. The Patent Office ruled in Farnsworth's favor. In 1939, RCA was finally forced to pay him and license his patents, the first time they had ever paid anyone for television technology. A teenage farm boy invented television, and this time, the little guy won.

description:
In 1927, 21-year-old American inventor Philo Farnsworth built the first working electronic television. RCA tried to steal the patent. He beat them in court anyway.
